headline: Uber lays off 10% of staff, cutting 3,300 jobs globally
summary: The ride-sharing giant is restructuring its management layers and consolidating divisions to invest more in its core services.
details: Uber has announced significant layoffs, cutting approximately 10% of its global workforce, which amounts to about 3,300 employees. The move is part of a broader restructuring effort aimed at streamlining operations and increasing efficiency.

The company's internal email, sent by CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, indicated a reduction in management layers by 20%, with some affected managers transitioning to individual contributor roles. This restructuring aims to simplify the organizational hierarchy.

Uber is also consolidating several divisions, including engineering, science, and delivery operations. This integration seeks to create more cohesive teams and improve coordination across its various business units, from ride-sharing to grocery and alcohol delivery.

As part of the restructuring, Uber is also phasing out most remote work opportunities. Only a small fraction, less than 1% of its staff, will be permitted to continue working remotely, signaling a shift towards a more in-office or hybrid work model for the majority of employees.

CEO Khosrowshahi cited the company's growth as a reason for increased complexity, stating that "growth has also brought complexity: more layers, more coordination, more fragmented ownership." The restructuring is intended to address these challenges and better serve the company at its current scale.
